title: De eximio usu methodi interpolationum in serierum doctrina

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Problem I of E555 (Opuscula analytica I, 1783). Euler wants an odd function y = αx + βx^3 + γx^5 + … that takes prescribed values y = p, q, r, s, … at x = a, b, c, d, …. Oddness then makes it also take the values −p, −q, … at −a, −b, ….

His ansatz is y = x[A + B(x²−a²) + C(x²−a²)(x²−b²) + …]. In modern terms this is Newton's divided-difference interpolation of g(u) = y/x in the variable u = x², with nodes u = a², b², c², ….

This page finishes the algorithm.
- Start from P = p/a, Q = q/b, R = r/c, ….
- Form successive divided differences: Q′ = (Q−P)/(b²−a²), R′ = (R−P)/(c²−a²), …; then R″ = (R′−Q′)/(c²−b²), …; then S‴ = (S″−R″)/(d²−c²), and so on.
- Each difference is taken against the first element of the previous column. This is a valid alternative scheme to the usual adjacent-node table.
- The coefficients are the diagonal: A = P, B = Q′, C = R″, D = S‴, E = T⁗.

Corollaries 1–3 (§§2–4) derive closed forms. B = p/(a(a²−b²)) + q/(b(b²−a²)). C and D are the symmetric sums Σ (p_i/a_i)/∏_{j≠i}(a_i²−a_j²). This is the Lagrange-type explicit formula for a divided difference, g[u_0,…,u_k] = Σ g(u_i)/∏_{j≠i}(u_i−u_j). Euler says the forms of E, F, G, … can be safely conjectured by induction.

The Scholion (§5) gives the recursive triangular solution of the fundamental equations: B = (q−bA)/(b(b²−a²)), C = (r−cA)/(c(c²−a²)(c²−b²)) − B/(c²−b²), and so on.

Purpose: in the next problems Euler sets p = sin a, etc. He lets x → 0 to get 1 = A − Ba² + Cа²b² − …, which yields sums giving π and related series. This is the 'eximius usus' of interpolation in the doctrine of series.
errors: No mathematical errors found on this page.
I checked the intermediate R″ expression, the unsimplified and simplified forms of C, and the Scholion recursions; all are correct.
The general formula for E, F, … is asserted by analogy ('tuto coniectura assequi licet') rather than proved; this is a minor gap.

ideas.what: Odd-function interpolation via Newton divided differences in the variable x² (y/x expanded in products (x²−a²)(x²−b²)…)
ideas.where_published: E555 itself; Euler also used Newton interpolation elsewhere (e.g. Institutiones calculi differentialis); details unsure

ideas.what: Explicit symmetric formula for each Newton coefficient: C = Σ p_i/(a_i ∏_{j≠i}(a_i²−a_j²))
ideas.modern_name: Explicit (Lagrange-form) expression of divided differences; partial-fraction form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange/Waring interpolation formula (Waring 1779, Lagrange 1795); divided-difference symmetric formula is standard (e.g. Ampère 1826)

ideas.what: Divided-difference table subtracting always the first entry of each column

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard Newton/Lagrange interpolation, specialized to odd functions and correctly worked out. The symmetric divided-difference formula slightly predates Lagrange's 1795 publication but is in line with Waring (1779) and well known. The paper is catalogued and known.
transcription_corrections: In the Scholion formula for E, the image's numerator '1−eA' should read 't−eA', consistent with the pattern.
Running headers read '160' and '161'; 'Euleri Opusc. Anal. Tom. I.' and signature 'X' are page furniture.
